info.name: Discord DMs Service
info.description: Discord DMs Service through the Gateway. Set base_url to the Gateway (http://localhost:8080) and service_token to the stack's SERVICE_TOKEN; every request carries the service prefix /api/v1/discord-dms. The Setup folder delivers session.started through POST /events as Session's relay would, so every run gets a fresh session. The WebSocket itself is opened outside Postman: folder 3 prints the ws_url to connect to directly.

7. Task timeout and concurrent task limit
GET /dev/slow?ms=7000 is stopped by the task timeout: 408 REQUEST_TIMEOUT

exec: pm.test('REQUEST_TIMEOUT with the timeout in details', () => { const e = pm.response.json().error; pm.expect(e.code).to.eql('REQUEST_TIMEOUT'); pm.expect(e.details.timeout_ms).to.be.a('number'); });
pm.test('answered at the service timeout (5 s), not after 7 s', () => pm.expect(pm.response.responseTime).to.be.below(6500));

request.description: The Gateway allows 10 s, the service 5 s: the service gives up first and the Gateway passes its 408 through unchanged.

item.name: the request above MAX_CONCURRENT_TASKS is refused at once: 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS

exec: // Fill every slot with slow tasks, then send the request above the limit and keep its answer for the tests.
for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) pm.sendRequest({ url: slow, method: 'GET', header: headers }, () => {});
// A moment for the burst to reach the service, then the one request too many.
pm.sendRequest({ url: pm.variables.get('base_url') + '/api/v1/discord-dms/dev/slow?ms=100', method: 'GET', header: headers }, (err, res) => {
let body = null; try { body = res.json(); } catch (e) {}
pm.variables.set('overflow', JSON.stringify({ error: err ? String(err) : null, status: res && res.code, retryAfter: res && res.headers.get('Retry-After'), body, ms: Date.now() - started }));
pm.test('the request above the limit got 429', () => { pm.expect(overflow.error, 'request error').to.eql(null); pm.expect(overflow.status).to.eql(429); });
pm.test('liveness stays exempt while the service is full', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description: The whole check runs from the scripts, because a script waits for its own pm.sendRequest calls before the request itself is sent: the pre-request fills every slot with slow tasks, sends one more shortly after and keeps its answer; the tests check that answer. The request of this item is only the liveness check, which stays exempt while the service is full.

item.name: after the burst the service accepts work again

exec: // Through the Gateway a player is identified by a JWT (HS256, JWT_SECRET shared with Player Service),
// never by X-Player-Id: the Gateway checks the token, discards any client-sent X-Player-Id and sets
// its own from the token's sub. Rather than logging in through Player Service, this script signs
// the token itself: every request that names a player in X-Player-Id gets
// Authorization: Bearer <jwt> with sub = that id, and the X-Player-Id header is dropped.
// jwt_secret must equal JWT_SECRET of the Gateway in the stack's .env.
const unsigned = part({ alg: 'HS256', typ: 'JWT' }) + '.' + part({ sub: sub, iat: now, exp: now + 300 });
